title: Governance: Who Sees What
brief: Given the Meridian access matrix — 4 personas across the core objects, one row filter
and four column masks — predict for 8 questions whether each user gets a full answer,
a masked answer, an empty answer, or a permission error. Then verify in the workspace.
Two of the eight are the interesting cases: the CFO who correctly sees zero rows, and
the regional lead who correctly sees the firm-wide total. Predicting those two is how
you show you understood the module.
An empty answer and a permission error are different outcomes, and Genie shows them
differently. Confusing the two is the most common mistake here.
NOTE ON GRADING. The predictions are the work, and a person reads them. The checks
below only confirm the governance objects exist to be tested against — they need
notebook 05_governance, which requires privileges you may not have.

checks.name: Prerequisite: the PII columns exist to be masked
sql: SELECT count(*) = 4 AS ok, concat(count(*), ' identifier columns found') AS detail
checks.hint: Run notebook 02. These four are what the column masks cover.

checks.name: Prerequisite: advisor region exists to filter rows on
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT region) = 4 AS ok, concat(count(DISTINCT region), ' regions') AS detail
checks.hint: NE, SE, MW and WEST. The row filter is applied on this column.

review: All 8 predictions are made BEFORE verifying in the workspace.
The CFO's zero rows is predicted, and explained as a row filter rather than missing data.
The regional lead's firm-wide total is predicted, and the reason is given.
An empty answer and a permission error are distinguished, not conflated.
